creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Every value of resize_step that parses produces the same maximal jump, because Muster and herdr disagree about the unit.

WHAT HERDR TAKES. pane.resize's `amount` is a fraction of the container, added straight to a split ratio - ~/src/herdr/src/layout.rs:235-237:

    let current_ratio = get_ratio_at(&self.root, &path).unwrap_or(0.5);
    let adj = if grows { delta } else { -delta };
    self.set_ratio_at(&path, current_ratio + adj);

and ~/src/herdr/src/app/api/panes.rs:404-409 defaults and clamps it:

    params.amount.filter(f32::is_finite).unwrap_or(0.05).abs().min(0.5)

So herdr's own step is 5% of the pane and its ceiling is 50%.

WHAT MUSTER SENDS. Cells. ResizeStep::cells (config.rs:267) converts points to cells, handler.rs:752 passes that as `amount`, and intent.rs:352 puts it on the wire unchanged. The doc comment on BackendIntent::ResizePane says 'in cells', which is simply not what the other side reads.

CONSEQUENCE. "10c" sends 10.0 and clamps to 0.5 - half the pane per press. And the SMALLEST expressible value does the same: "1c" sends 1.0, and "1px" is floored to one cell by ResizeStep::cells, so it also sends 1.0. The key therefore has exactly one behaviour for every input a person can write, and omitting it - which sends no amount and gets herdr's 5% - is the only way to a usable step. That is why this felt fine before the key existed.

HOW IT GOT PAST EVERYTHING. corpus/conformance/backend-intent.json pins only that the number is passed through, and its own case names the field `ratio` while the intent doc says cells - the disagreement is visible in the corpus and nothing compares either against herdr. No recording in docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md says what `amount` means, so the unit was assumed rather than measured. Worth an observation entry either way.

THE FIX, AND THE DECISION IN IT. A distance in points or cells becomes a fraction only against the extent it is a fraction OF, and Muster does not know which extent herdr will use: herdr adjusts the NEAREST split's ratio, and that split's node area is the whole region only when there is one split on that axis. Two routes:

1. Approximate. Have the shell report the region's extent along the axis (it already reports cell_width/cell_height on ResizePane), and send points/extent. Exact for a single split per axis, under-moves in nested layouts. Small change, strictly better than today.
2. Exact. Derive the split path from layout.export and use layout.set_split_ratio, which observations section (border ids / resize API) says takes that same path. Precise at every depth, and a much bigger change that means Muster holding a tree.

Route 1 with the inaccuracy stated is probably right for now; the config vocabulary ("20c" / "150px") does not have to change either way, which is the point of it being a distance.

MEANWHILE amterp's ~/.muster/config.toml has the key commented out with a pointer here.
title: 🎚️ resize_step is sent as cells, and herdr reads a fraction
